close_reason: fixed: update_object failure triggers destroy_object rollback; comment explains pattern
description: In handle_vacation_set (vacation.rs lines 185-225), when update_object returns NotFound the handler creates the singleton and immediately applies the patch via a second update_object call. If that second update_object call returns BackendSetError::SetError (line 211), the handler inserts into not_updated and continues — but the singleton object was already created (line 187-189). The state is now inconsistent: the singleton exists in storage but the client sees notUpdated. On the next call, update_object will succeed, so the client's patch is silently lost. The fix is to either not_updated with a clear description, or to not insert the not_updated entry when the second update fails after a successful create (which would be confusing in a different way). The code comment on line 179 acknowledges the concurrent-creation race but not this second-update failure path.
title: VacationResponse/set upsert: create_object success but second update_object SetError leaves orphan singleton
